summary: Feature baseline for OWASP Juice Shop 20.2.0. Covers the features a shopper actually uses: register, log in, search, basket, addresses, payment cards, order history, contact and language. Each endpoint that the UI calls is covered at both the API layer and the browser layer, because a direct call proves the server handles the payload the test chose, not that the app sends it. Failures here are the bug list for step 2.

riskAreas.reason: GET /rest/basket/:id takes an id from the URL and the source shows no ownership check next to the handler
routes/login.ts concatenates req.body.email into raw SQL with no validation
routes/search.ts truncates q to 200 chars then concatenates it into a LIKE clause
the app was observed requesting /rest/basket/NaN and /rest/track-order/undefined during a normal authenticated crawl
four handlers are registered on POST /api/Users at server.ts lines 427, 439, 440, 441

cases.title: A new account can be registered
cases.why: registration is the entry point to every other feature
steps: POST /api/Users with a unique email, password, passwordRepeat, securityQuestion and securityAnswer
cases.expected: 201, and the response body contains the new user id and email

cases.title: Registering with an email that already exists is rejected
cases.why: duplicate accounts on one email break login and password reset
steps: POST /api/Users again with the same email
cases.expected: a 4xx status, not 201, and no second user is created

cases.title: Valid credentials return a token
cases.why: every authenticated feature depends on this
steps: POST /rest/user/login with the registered email and password
cases.expected: 200 and body authentication.token is a non-empty string, authentication.bid is a number

cases.title: A wrong password is rejected
cases.why: the negative path of the only auth gate
steps: POST /rest/user/login with the registered email and the wrong password
cases.expected: 401, and no token in the body

cases.title: A user can log in through the login form
cases.why: proves the form sends what the server expects, which a direct call cannot prove
steps: Wait for the login button to become enabled
cases.expected: the POST /rest/user/login request returns 200 and the account menu shows the logged in user

cases.title: The login form shows an error for wrong credentials
cases.why: a 401 the user never sees is a broken feature
steps: Enter a valid email and a wrong password
cases.expected: an error message is visible to the user and the app stays on the login page

cases.title: The login form handles a server error
cases.why: the source passes handler errors to next(), so a 500 is reachable in production
steps: Intercept POST /rest/user/login and fulfil it with 500
Open #/login and submit valid looking credentials
cases.expected: the user sees an error message, the page does not hang on a spinner and does not go blank

cases.title: Search returns matching products
cases.why: search is the main way a shopper finds anything
cases.expected: 200 and every returned product has name or description containing the term

cases.title: An empty search term returns the full catalogue rather than an error
cases.why: the source treats the literal string undefined and an absent q as empty
cases.expected: 200 in both cases and a non-empty product list

cases.title: A search term with no matches returns an empty list, not an error
cases.why: the empty result path is where LIKE based search usually breaks
cases.expected: 200 and an empty data array

cases.title: A quote in the search term does not break the query
cases.why: the source concatenates q into a LIKE clause with no escaping
cases.expected: 200 with a valid result list, not a 500 and not a database error in the body

cases.title: Searching from the header returns results on the page
cases.why: proves the UI sends the term the server expects
cases.expected: the GET /rest/products/search request fires with q=apple and matching products render

cases.title: Search shows an empty state rather than a blank page
cases.why: empty state handling is invisible until the list is empty
steps: Intercept GET /rest/products/search and fulfil with 200 and an empty data array
cases.expected: the page tells the user nothing was found, and does not render an empty grid with no message

cases.title: A logged in user can read their own basket
cases.why: the core of the shopping flow
steps: Log in and read authentication.bid from the response
cases.expected: 200 and data.UserId is the logged in user's id

cases.title: A user cannot read another user's basket
cases.why: the source shows no ownership check on this route
steps: Register user A and user B
cases.expected: 403 or 404. A must not receive B's basket contents

cases.title: A basket id that does not exist is rejected
cases.why: the app was seen requesting /rest/basket/NaN during a normal crawl
cases.expected: 404 for the missing id and 400 for the non-numeric ones. Not 200 with a success status and null data

cases.title: The basket page shows the user's items
cases.why: proves the page requests the right basket for the logged in user
cases.expected: the GET /rest/basket/{id} request uses the logged in user's own bid and the items render

cases.title: The basket page handles a failed load
cases.why: error handling on the most used authenticated page
cases.expected: an error is shown to the user and the page does not stay on a spinner

cases.title: Order history loads for a logged in user
cases.why: only reachable once logged in, so it is easy to leave untested
cases.expected: 200 and a data array

cases.title: Order history requires authentication
cases.why: order history contains personal purchase data
cases.expected: 401, and no order data in the body

cases.title: An unknown order id is rejected
cases.why: the app was seen requesting /rest/track-order/undefined during a normal crawl
cases.expected: 404 or an empty result. Not 200 with status success and the literal id echoed back as a real order

cases.title: Addresses require authentication
cases.why: addresses are personal data and only appeared in the authenticated crawl
cases.expected: 401, and no address data

cases.title: The saved addresses page lists the user's addresses
cases.why: proves the page calls the endpoint with the right auth
cases.expected: GET /api/Addresss returns 200 and the page renders the list or an explicit empty state

cases.title: Payment cards require authentication
cases.why: card data is the most sensitive thing in the app
cases.expected: 401, and no card data

cases.title: The language list loads
cases.why: the header language menu depends on it on every page
cases.expected: 200 and a non-empty array that includes en

cases.title: The app still renders when the language list fails
cases.why: this call fires on every page, so a failure would be site wide
cases.expected: the page still renders in the default language and does not go blank

cases.title: The application configuration loads
cases.why: requested on five different pages, so the whole UI depends on it
cases.expected: 200 and a config object

cases.title: A captcha is issued for the contact form
cases.why: the contact form cannot be submitted without it
cases.expected: 200 with a captcha question and an id

cases.title: The contact page loads its captcha
cases.why: proves the page requests and renders the captcha it needs
cases.expected: GET /rest/captcha/ returns 200 and the captcha question is visible on the form

cases.title: whoami returns the logged in user
cases.why: the app uses this to decide whether a session is still valid
steps: GET /rest/user/whoami with a valid bearer token
cases.expected: 200 and the body contains the logged in user's email and id

cases.title: whoami returns no user when not authenticated
cases.why: if this leaked a user for an anonymous caller the whole session model would be wrong
cases.expected: an empty user object or a 401. No email, id or role for an anonymous caller

cases.title: The contact page identifies the logged in user
cases.why: proves the page sends the session the server expects
cases.expected: GET /rest/user/whoami returns 200 and the form is prefilled for the logged in user

cases.title: Every page loads the application configuration
cases.why: five different pages request it, so a failure would be site wide
cases.expected: GET /rest/admin/application-configuration returns 200 on each page and the branding and titles render from it

cases.title: The version endpoint returns a version string
cases.why: the UI displays it and support uses it to identify a build
cases.expected: 200 and a non-empty version string

cases.title: The version is shown in the UI
cases.why: a version the user can never see is not a feature
cases.expected: the version from the endpoint appears somewhere in the page

cases.title: Product quantities load
cases.why: the product list uses it to show stock and to block over-ordering
cases.expected: 200 and an array where each row has a ProductId and a quantity

cases.title: The product list reflects stock
cases.why: proves the page uses the quantity data it fetches
steps: Open the app and wait for the product grid
cases.expected: GET /api/Quantitys/ returns 200 and products render with their stock state

cases.title: The challenge list is readable
cases.why: this run uses it as the independent oracle for whether a bug is really fixed, so it must be reliable
cases.expected: 200 and 116 challenges, each with a name, category and solved flag

cases.title: The score board renders the challenge list
cases.why: the page exists and calls the endpoint, so it is part of the feature surface
cases.expected: GET /api/Challenges/ returns 200 and challenges render on the page
